pictures.scene: Ancher, Sunshine in the Blind Woman's Room — an old blind woman standing alone at the end of a scrubbed table in a low cottage room, the sun pouring in through a small window at the right and throwing two bright yellow squares of light onto the wall behind her, one of them falling across her shoulder, her face lifted a little toward the window with the eyes clouded and sightless, a dark headcloth tied close over her hair, a heavy black dress with a worn blue green jacket showing at one sleeve, one hand resting flat on the table and the other hanging at her side, the deep shadow of her head thrown on the wall beside her, a glowing yellow bowl, a ball of wool and a few small things lying on the sunlit window sill, and in front of her a dark wooden chair and a bare plank floor, he saw a man blind from birth, …
pictures.name: pd_ancher_solskin_i_den_blindes_stue

pictures.scene: Church, Twilight in the Wilderness — the last of the daylight going out over an empty mountain country, the whole upper two thirds of the picture a sky of burning cloud, long ragged banks of scarlet and crimson streaming across the top and breaking into smaller flecks and ripples, a wide sweep of dark olive grey cloud under them, a few bars of hot orange lower down, and along the horizon a band of clear pale green and gold where the sun has just gone, below that a low range of blue violet hills with a wooded ridge closing in on either side, and at the bottom a still lake lying in shadow with the red of the sky reflected in a long streak down it, a tiny wooded island with two dead firs standing on it, and dark spruce and rock crowding the near shore, night is coming, when no one can work, …
pictures.name: pd_church_twilight_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Cavallino, a young saint with the eyes lifted — a single young figure seen close and from just below, standing against a plain dim grey brown wall with the shadow of the head thrown across it, the whole face turned upward into the light and strongly modelled, the lips parted, the eyes wide and raised as though something has only just been given back to them, dark hair falling in loose waves at the temples, one bare hand held up open beside the face with two fingers raised, a loose olive green tunic with a plain white under shirt showing at the open neck, a heavy vermilion mantle gathered over the arm and falling down the right side of the picture, and held low in the lap on the edge of a closed book a shallow pewter dish, so the man went and washed, and came back seeing, …
pictures.name: pd_cavallino_ogen

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Beggars — a little group of crippled beggars out on the grass beside a high brick wall, the ground a worn green turf and the wall and a dark wooden outbuilding filling the top of the panel, one of them at the left propped on a wooden crutch and staring up out of the picture with his mouth open, a knitted cap on his head, a black hood round his shoulders and a long white tabard hung with foxtails over his dark coat, another sitting square in front of us with his back turned and a tall white paper cap on his head, his white tabard likewise sewn with foxtails, his crutch under one arm and his legs cut short so that the stumps are bound into two padded leather pattens on the grass, a third pushing himself along at the right on a short stick, and behind them a woman in a long black cloak and a flat grey hat walking away with an empty begging bowl held out in one hand, isn't this the man who used to sit and beg, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Van Everdingen, waterfall with a mill — a mountain torrent breaking over a ledge of rock and falling in white water down the whole middle of the picture, a strip of grey and white cloud with a patch of blue along the top, dark spruces and a wooden church tower standing up on the skyline, a thatched hut on the left bank and a long timber mill shed with a broken shingled roof on the right, two small figures standing up by the sluice where the water is let through, a rough plank footbridge with a handrail crossing the gorge low on the left, great wet brown boulders and a fallen beam lying in the flood, and at the bottom the stream running on white and broken between the rocks, so i went and washed and received my sight, …
pictures.name: pd_everdingen_bron

pictures.scene: Delaroche, a prisoner questioned in her cell — an old churchman in a great scarlet robe sitting square in the left half of the picture and filling it from top to bottom, a red cap on his head, a heavy gold cross hanging on his breast, white linen sleeves showing at the wrists, one hand gripping the arm of his chair and the other thrust out flat over his knee as he leans forward and turns his hard lined face toward the prisoner, behind him at the very edge another man in shadow holding up a written paper, and at the right a young woman sitting low on a bed of loose straw against the bare stone wall of the cell, her dark hair down, a plain white shift with dark sleeves, a black iron band locked on her wrist and a chain running down from it across her lap, her hands folded together and her eyes lifted away from him, a wide black emptiness of cell wall filling the whole top of the picture and a cold grey floor below, they brought to the pharisees the man who had been blind, …
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Sabbath Rest — a quiet olive green room on the day of rest, a tall window with small panes in the middle of the picture hung with a looped lace curtain and a pale grey town showing through it, a heavy brass sabbath lamp hanging on its chain from the ceiling at the top, a framed picture on the wall at the right, a man in a dark coat and a blue cap sitting under the window and holding an open book up in both hands as he reads, an old man with a white beard dozing in a chair at the left edge with a child asleep across his lap, a young woman in a loose coral wrap standing behind them with her eyes lowered, two more figures seen from behind at the right in dark shawls beside a wooden cabinet, and a bare worn floor across the bottom, now the day on which jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a sabbath, …
pictures.name: pd_hirszenberg_sabbath_rest

pictures.scene: Hart, The Rejoicing of the Law — the inside of an old synagogue on a feast day, worked stone arches and a vaulted ceiling across the top with two big silver lamps hanging down on long chains, a white carved and painted railing running across the middle with tall candlesticks and lit candles standing on it, bearded elders in prayer shawls and two boys leaning over the rail to watch, a man in a wide black hat and a striped white shawl standing in the middle of the floor carrying a scroll of the law in a scarlet cover with silver bells on its staves, two more men behind him at the left carrying scrolls in blue and crimson covers, others in tall caps and long coats crowding in at the left edge, an old man in red seated at a dark reading desk on the right, and a pale tiled pavement across the bottom, and there was division among them, …
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Mijtens, a family out of doors — a father and mother with their two children posed under a great tree, the huge rough trunk and a spread of dark leaves filling the right side and the top corner, a pale clouded sky and far blue wooded hills showing between the branches at the left, the father standing in a heavy dark coat with a deep crimson cloak wrapped across him and a plain white collar at his throat, his long curled hair falling to his shoulders and one hand laid on his breast, the mother seated beside him in a wide silver white satin gown with pearls at her neck and in her hair, reaching out one hand to the small boy at her knee, the boy standing in a long blue silk dress with a white sash and a feathered hat, holding up a bunch of grapes, and a baby sitting on her lap wrapped in a rose coloured cloth with a little wreath of flowers on its head, a small dog at the lower right, and bare brown earth across the bottom, is this your son, the one you say was born blind, …
pictures.name: pd_mijtens_gezin

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, an old man in red — one very old man sitting alone in a high backed wooden chair, the whole ground around him a deep warm brown that goes almost black at the top, the light falling only on his face and on his two hands, his forehead creased and heavy, the eyes sunk and shadowed and looking steadily out, a long white beard spreading down over his chest, a soft dark cap on his head, a loose red robe of heavy cloth hanging in deep folds from his shoulders with the light running along its edge, a dark cloak over one shoulder, and his two big worn hands folded quietly together in his lap, he is old enough to speak for himself, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_old_man

pictures.scene: Gottlieb, praying in the synagogue on the day of atonement — a crowd packed close together under low stone arches, every face brought up large and near, a bearded man in a tall fur hat in the middle of the picture holding a scroll of the law against him in both arms, its pale cover worked with a six pointed star and lines of hebrew, a young man at the right with his hand pressed to his forehead and his eyes almost shut, another man at the left bowed down over an open book on the reading desk with his hand at his temple, an older man behind them in a white and black striped prayer shawl staring out, a gallery of women above at the back leaning on the rail in headcloths and embroidered shawls, a pale window and a teal curtain glowing behind them, a solemn faced boy in a flowered coat standing at the lower left, and striped shawls hanging to the floor all across the front, would be put out of the synagogue, …
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Millais, The Blind Girl — a blind beggar girl sitting out in a wide meadow after rain with a little sister leaning against her, the grass burning acid green in the sun and running back to a low hill with cattle, a white horse and sheep grazing on it, a village of red roofed houses and a church tower on the ridge, a slate blue storm sky still dark along the top with a double rainbow standing clear across it, the blind girl in a worn brown cloak drawn over her head and a wide gold brown skirt, her eyes closed and her face turned up to feel the warmth, a small card hung at her throat, a concertina lying shut in her lap and a blade of grass held between her fingers, a tortoiseshell butterfly resting unseen on her shawl, the younger girl in a dark green jacket and a blue skirt turning to look back at the rainbow with her hand holding the cloak up over her hair, and rough tussocks and a wet rut in the grass at the bottom, i was blind, but now i see, …
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_blind_girl

pictures.scene: Breu, the crowd shouting against Him — a press of priests and elders crowded hard against one another and all talking at once, a high priest at the left in a jewelled white and gold mitre and a yellow mantle over a green robe, leaning forward with both hands raised and the fingers counting off his argument, a bald man in a black cap and a white fur collar standing in front of him in a wide scarlet robe with gold embroidered sleeves, his face turned up and his mouth open as he shouts back, a rolled paper gripped in his hand, a second mitred priest at the right edge with a long black beard looking out at us, behind them a bank of angry faces in red, green and white caps and turbans with their mouths open and bare arms thrown up above their heads, a bare dark wall at the top left, and worked pale stone steps cutting across the whole lower left corner, what did he do to you, how did he open your eyes, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Champaigne, Moses with the tablets of the law — one huge old man brought right up to the front of the picture against a plain black ground, his head and shoulders filling the upper half, two short beams of light standing up out of his hair like horns, a long grey gold beard spreading over his chest, his mouth a little open and his eyes turned sharply to one side as though he has just been spoken to, a deep blue mantle with gold embroidered bands over a dark gold brocaded tunic and a soft pink shirt showing at the cuff, a long thin gilt rod lying across him from shoulder to hand, his big veined hand resting on a grey stone ledge at the bottom, and standing upright beside him the two tall stone tablets of the commandments, numbered and written out line by line in dark lettering down the whole left side of the picture, we are disciples of moses, …
pictures.name: pd_champaigne_moses_with_the_ten_commandments

pictures.scene: Victors, an old woman praying in the temple — one elderly woman shown close and half length against the dim grey stone of a temple hall, a dark doorway and a pale column standing behind her, her lined face lifted and turned slightly up into the light with the lips parted as though she is speaking her prayer aloud, a wide pleated hat of orange and dark red set on her head and a long dark veil falling from under it on both sides, a stiff white pleated collar gathered at her throat with a small gold stud, a heavy gown of red brown silk with broad bands of fur across the shoulders and gold patterned cuffs at the wrists, and her two old hands pressed tightly together and folded one over the other in the middle of the picture, he does listen to the one who worships him, …
pictures.name: pd_victors_hanna_biddend_in_de_tempel

pictures.scene: Friedrich, a woman before the rising sun — one woman standing alone on an open heath with her back to us and her face turned away into the light, the whole sky above her a deep burning gold that pales toward the horizon where the sun is coming up behind a low range of brown hills, her figure a dark full length silhouette rising from the bottom of the picture almost to the top, a long high waisted dress falling straight to the ground, her hair pinned up in a comb, and both arms held out and open at her sides with the hands turned up and the light catching the fingers, dark heather, scattered stones and a bare track in the ground around her feet, and fine craquelure over the whole surface, never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_woman_rising_sun

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, an old man grieving — one old man sitting alone on a plain rush seated wooden chair in a bare room, bent right over with his elbows on his knees and both fists pressed hard against his face so that nothing of it can be seen, his bald head and a fringe of white hair catching the light, dressed from neck to ankle in a worn blue working suit painted in long ridged strokes with every seam drawn in darker blue, heavy laced boots on his feet set flat on the boards, a small fire of red and orange burning in the grate at the left edge beside him, the pale wall behind him worked in blue and white strokes, and a plank floor streaked with blue, green and cream running away under the chair, and they threw him out, …
pictures.name: pd_vangogh_eternitys_gate

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ and the woman at the well — Christ sitting on the low stone kerb of a well out in the evening country and talking with a woman who has come to draw water, a grey blue sky with a bar of cloud across the top of the panel, a broken brick tower and dark ivied walls behind on the left, a great mass of dark foliage and a palm leaved tree in the middle, Christ turned toward her in a long red brown robe with a dark mantle over his shoulder, his hair falling loose and one hand lifted and pointing away to the left as he speaks, the woman standing at the right in a white blouse with full sleeves, a red band in her hair and a long yellow skirt, leaning both hands on the pale stone rim of the well with the well rope looped over it and her face lowered as she listens, a few small figures of his companions coming up in the shadow at the left edge, and the painted edge of the panel showing top and bottom, he is the one speaking with you, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_and_the_woman_from_samaria

pictures.scene: Veronese, Christ and the centurion — a soldier kneeling down in the street in front of Christ and pleading with him, Christ standing on the left in a rose red tunic and a dark blue mantle with a thin gold ring of light at his hair, his head bent and his eyes lowered toward the kneeling man, his feet bare on the pavement, two disciples pressing close behind him and an old white bearded man and a bald man looking down over his shoulder, the soldier on one knee at the right in polished steel armour with gilt edging and a great crimson cloak spread over his legs, his head thrown back and his bearded face turned up to Christ, one hand held against his breast while an officer in a plumed and gilded helmet steadies him from behind, a second soldier standing above them holding a tall halberd, a pale domed building and a grey sky showing at the back on the right, and a dark stone pavement at the bottom, lord, i believe, he said, and he worshiped jesus, …
pictures.name: pd_veronese_centurion

pictures.scene: Durer, Christ among the Doctors — a close press of heads and hands crowded right up against the picture plane on a near-black ground, the young Christ in the middle in a blue-green robe with long waving red-gold hair and a faint rayed halo, His eyes lowered and His face calm as He counts off His argument by pinching one finger of His left hand with His right, a bald old doctor leaning in at the right with his mouth dragged open and his broken teeth showing as he shouts into the argument, his wrinkled hands thrust across in front of Christ with the fingers spread and counting back at Him, a second very old man with a long white beard pushing in at the lower right and holding up a thick vellum book with his gnarled hand on the boards, a third man at the upper left clipped by the edge with a clasped volume open in his fist, and more hands and a book coming in at the lower left, are we blind too, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_onderwijst

lines.text: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth, and His disciples asked Him, Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?
Jesus answered, Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.
While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man's eyes.
Then He told him, Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam which means Sent. So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.
At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?
Some claimed that he was, but others said, No, he just looks like him. But the man kept saying, I am the one.
How then were your eyes opened? they asked.
He answered, The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.
Where is He? they asked. I do not know, he answered.
They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. The man answered, He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.
Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath. But others said, How can a sinful man perform such signs? And there was division among them.
So once again they asked the man who had been blind, What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened? He is a prophet, the man replied.
The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents
and asked, Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?
His parents answered, We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.
But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
That was why his parents said, He is old enough. Ask him.
So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.
He answered, Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!
What did He do to you? they asked. How did He open your eyes?
He replied, I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?
Then they heaped insults on him and said, You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.
We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.
That is remarkable indeed! the man said. You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.
If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.
They replied, You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us? And they threw him out.
When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, Do you believe in the Son of Man?
Who is He, Sir? he replied. Tell me so that I may believe in Him.
You have already seen Him, Jesus answered. He is the One speaking with you.
Lord, I believe, he said. And he worshiped Jesus.
Then Jesus declared, For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.
Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, Are we blind too?
If you were blind, Jesus replied, you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.
